scene_design:
Variant design: A forms the LEFT wing, a two-storey compact housing/service block. Its lower facade consists of a rounded recessed service bay and broad reclaimed wraparound actuator casings with a deep utility spine, occupying about40% of the first-floor visible walls. The upper dwelling is a chunky rounded-corner module projecting over a narrower structural waist, with a deep inset window, substantial brackets, and one recessed mechanical band/duct around20% of upper facade. At ground level shallow rounded corners blend into short axis-aligned work ledges/supports, leaving no broad walkable-looking corner pocket behind an invisible rectangular wall. Give A a stepped roof silhouette with a raised louvered service spine and attached broad utility canopy/maintenance deck taking roughly half its roof, no common solar/tank kit.
B occupies the rear RIGHT corner: wide ground-level scrap workshop, with the upper home exactly half the workshop footprint, offset to its LEFT half. The upper home has a short asymmetric pitched roof with a large salvage ventilation dormer and a supported service canopy. A broad projecting workshop awning, recessed shutter bay and different wall-depth zones give the lower storey a different silhouette. Open remaining terrace carries a grounded salvaged hoist base and sorted stock behind a railing; the house plus purposeful terrace elements occupy40–80% of lower roof, the house's own supported dormer/canopy around half its roof. A small supported access stair/landing connects the house to the workshop side. B's shutter and household door are closed ordinary entries, NOT extra map exits.
C is on the RIGHT near-front wing, a low one-storey repair shed with a distinctly stepped SAWTOOTH / north-light roof, a wide asymmetrical entrance canopy and deep human door. Raised ventilation/light monitors and a roof-mounted repair canopy make its roof functional over roughly half its area without piling tanks on it. Beside C, toward the back, a large upright recycled heat-exchanger / pressure-buffer machine with a heavy support frame and visible replacement connector forms part of the rear-right barrier. It is not a fourth building. A high supported service conduit bridges only the narrow peripheral connection, never low across the center.
LEFT functional transition: a visible external STAIR immediately to the right of A ascends along the Y axis to a real landing and an upper service passage toward the rear-left boundary. Show substantial stair stringers, adequate width, railings and clear landing; the designated upper door is closed with sensible sliding travel into its wall pocket and unobstructed approach. A's ordinary ground door is not another map transition. RIGHT functional transition: an OPEN ground-level service alley between C and the upright mechanical assembly leading toward the rear-right boundary, under a sufficiently high supported conduit. Its entrance, whole clear passage and outward continuation read together; it is defined by building/machinery, not a new masonry wall gate.
Remaining rear gaps are stopped by mechanically anchored closed scrap-bin bodies, machine housings and short heavy fences that meet the buildings, with no accidental third routes beneath or between them. Keep the center free with a readable alley elbow and outer perimeter detail, not a huge empty plaza. Front foundation: visibly different from variant1, large reclaimed masonry bays with a sealed modular power-distribution bank embedded in the left face and a heavy horizontal drainage drum in the right; neither is walkable. Keep the square slab sharp, straight-sided and constant-depth, with entire cutaways visible.
Form sources: INPUT4 is attachment3, for the supported larger upper module and recessed middle-storey depth. INPUT5 is attachment6, for large integrated utility channels, deep panel layering and building-scale mechanical form. Adapt them into an older repaired settlement with selective mismatched replacement parts, not a pristine corporate SF block.
